title: Active Mortgage Loan Files per Customer and per Property
content:
**Rule.** A customer may have at most 2 Mortgage Loan Files in a non-terminal status at the same time, counted across every Larkspur loan file on which the customer is the primary borrower. The non-terminal statuses are application received, disclosed, processing, underwriting, conditionally approved, suspended and clear to close; consummated, withdrawn, denied and closed-incomplete files do not count. A new application that would exceed the cap is not opened.

**Same property.** No other loan file of the same customer for the same property address is in a non-terminal status. A borrower who wants a different program or amount on a property already in process keeps the existing file and changes its program or terms instead of opening a second file. The check reads the system's loan file records for the customer — the primary borrower, the property address exactly as on the purchase contract or title, and the file status — before a new file is opened; a file's loan purpose does not distinguish two files for the same property.

## Status counting

| File status | Counts toward the limit of 2 | Blocks a second file at the same address |
|---|---|---|
| application received, disclosed, processing, underwriting, conditionally approved, suspended, clear to close | yes | yes |
| consummated, withdrawn, denied, closed incomplete | no | no |

## Cases (hypothetical customers)

- A customer is primary borrower on one file in underwriting for 12 Elm Street and one consummated file from an earlier purchase. One file counts, so a new application for a different address may be opened; it would be the second counting file.
- A customer has one file in processing and one suspended file, both for different addresses. Two files count, so a third application is not opened.
- A customer has a file in conditionally approved status for 40 Oak Avenue and asks to apply again for 40 Oak Avenue as a rate-and-term refinance instead of a purchase. The existing file for that address is non-terminal, so no second file is opened for it; the existing file's program or terms are changed instead.
